thread:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Rolling deploy started: service=inference-api, target=prod, version=v3.4-canary, canary=10% — tracking in <https://console.redwood.internal/deploys/3987>
morgan: seeing a bump in 5xx on the canary shard (~2:10pm). error-rate p50->p95 jump, cpu fine but tails spiking. sending traces now.
oncall-bot: Paging user(s): @santiago — urgent incident triggered: inference-api 5xx spike on canary (alert: infra.alerts.5xx_rate > 1% over 5m)
santiago: oncall here, looking. morgan can you paste the query + one sample trace? also are any customer-facing errors flagged?
morgan: sample metric: 5xx rate on canary nodes = 3.8% (baseline prod non-canary 0.1%). trace id 0x9f3a — stack shows LLM-serving grpc timeout -> upstream retry loop. quick log snippet:

```
2026-03-15T14:10:22Z inference-api v3.4 ERROR request_id=0x9f3a upstream_connect_timeout: attempt=3 grpc deadline exceeded
  at runtime/serve.go:412
```

elaine: we have two customers in monitoring (acme-inc, beta-shop) reporting increased latency and intermittent 500s. CS alerted and opened tickets.
katie: looks like the new routing change (enable-v3-routing) was rolled out with the canary. recommend kill-switch if traffic-level rollback takes time.
santiago: agree. first step: stop escalation — cut canary traffic back to 0 and revert routing. who can flip the flag? elaine, can you do LD toggle? otherwise i'll run manual routing change.
elaine: flipping LaunchDarkly flag now: enable-v3-routing -> false. request_id LD-7123. will confirm.
elaine: :white_check_mark: flag toggled. traffic to v3.4 dropped to 0% according to router metrics. but 5xx still lingering on some nodes (probably sticky sessions).
morgan: seeing some draining nodes still reporting errors 2-3%. might be connection pooling to upstream. suggestion: initiate manual rollback of the deployment (kubectl) to previous stable revision.
santiago: ok plan: 1) flip feature flag (done), 2) manual rollback of inference-api to v3.3 on prod, 3) run smoke + canary checks, 4) confirm customer impact cleared, 5) postmortem ops notes. who will run the kubectl rollback?
katie: I can do the rollback in the next 2 mins. will coordinate with morgan for smoke tests.
katie: running:

```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/inference-api --to-revision=42
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/inference-api
```

katie: rollout started. current pods terminating, new pods coming up.
morgan: running quick smoke: /health, /v1/predict sample load, tokenize + forward. also checking kv-cache warmup.
morgan: smoke results: health OK on all new pods, baseline latency restored to p50=120ms p95=400ms, 5xx ~0.05%.
santiago: good. begin staged traffic increase to confirm stability. katie, hold incremental traffic to 5% for 10 mins then 25%.
katie: bumped to 5% at 14:25 — monitoring dashboards in <https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/inference-api>
(5 minutes pass)
morgan: at 5% still stable. no new 5xx alerts. traces show no grpc timeout patterns.
santiago: proceed to 25%.
katie: bumped to 25% at 14:31.
(another 8 minutes)
elaine: CS reports reduced alerts from customers, tickets updated: acme-inc marked as "mitigated". Beta-shop still had one request fail earlier but not since rollback.
morgan: continued monitoring metrics: error-rate back to baseline cluster-wide. pushing verifying smoke set (run full integration test harness now).

```
# quick verification script (run by morgan)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMOKE_TOKEN" https://inference-api.prod.internal/v1/health
python tests/smoke_run.py --model=llama2 --n=200 --max_tokens=128
```

morgan: smoke harness completed: 200 requests, 0 failures, latency p95 420ms. all checks green.
santiago: escalation closed. will leave the deploy in rollback state and mark the release blocked until follow-up bug triage.
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Rollback completed: service=inference-api rolled back to v3.3 (revision=42). duration=13m. links: <https://console.redwood.internal/deploys/3987>, <https://console.redwood.internal/incidents/1987654322>
santiago: thanks team. next steps: research root cause (likely grpc upstream timeout under new routing), run local repro, reproduce with load profile, and triage in postmortem. assigning to morgan + eng-ml + eng-runtime.
morgan: starting a debug branch and will capture core dumps + long-tail traces. will ping when I have a reproducer.
elaine: CS notified customers and updated incident status. will share postmortem draft once we have root cause and timeline.
santiago: closing thread here. good job on fast mitigation; file follow-up tasks in JIRA: INF-5493 (repro), INF-5494 (rollback playbook updates), INF-5495 (routing validation tests). :thumbsup:
